title: Shapes the amiga-re project documents share
description: Identities, digests, addresses, and path safety. Every other project schema references these rather than restating them, so one rule cannot be tightened in one document and left loose in another.

formatVersion.description: The contract version this document is written against. All documents in a project must use the same supported format version.

id.description: A project-wide identity: a required kind prefix, a colon, then a readable name. Never a path, a display name, an array index, an address, or a content hash — it must survive renaming the file and improving the label.

relativePath.description: A project-relative path: UTF-8, `/`-separated, never absolute, never containing `.` or `..` as a component. The only spelling a document may use, so a project describes the same thing on every host.

hexAddress.description: A runtime address as fixed-form lowercase hexadecimal. A string because JSON has no hex integer syntax and addresses are reviewed as hex; parsers range-check every conversion.

origin.description: Where a piece of knowledge came from. Only `user` and `reviewed_analysis` are durable claims; `imported` records that another tool asserted it.

confidence.description: The same vocabulary the semantic fact report uses, so a promoted fact keeps its meaning.

extensions.description: Project-specific data the toolkit neither validates nor interprets. The one place unknown keys are allowed; everything else is closed.

objectRange.description: A byte range in an object's own offsets.

hunkRange.description: A byte range within one hunk of a parsed image.

runtimeRange.description: An address range under one named load map. Meaningless without the map, which is why it is named rather than assumed.

entityTarget.description: Attaches to another annotation rather than to bytes, so renaming or rebasing that annotation carries this one with it.

baseRegisterSlot.description: A small-data global at a base-register displacement — the shape `disasm globals` reports and nothing could previously name. It is a location in the loaded program rather than a range in the file, so it carries no offset or length; the access width is the size of the slot itself. The image and the object digest are carried like every other byte target, so a global goes stale when the bytes it was established against change.

base_register.description: The address register the displacement is taken from — A4 or A5 by convention, but stated rather than assumed.

displacement.description: The signed 16-bit displacement, as the addressing mode encodes it.

width.description: The access width in bytes: a byte, word, or longword slot.

storageTarget.description: Where a value lives: the four spaces that name bytes, and not `entity`. A variable's storage has to be somewhere a width can be measured, and an entity target deliberately covers no bytes of its own — it attaches to another annotation, whose bytes are that annotation's. A global at an absolute address is a `runtime` or `hunk` target here; the base-register slot is one shape of shared state rather than the only one.

target.description: Where an annotation applies. Tagged by `space` so a file offset, a hunk offset, a runtime address, and a base-register slot can never be confused for one another. Every byte target carries the object digest it was established against: if the bytes change the annotation is stale and must be rebased explicitly, never silently reapplied to the same number.
